title: Enforce JSON-mode responses and constrained decoding for structured-output APIs; add schema adherence test-suite
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Add a robust, runtime-enforced JSON mode and constrained-decoding pipeline for Redwood's text-generation API so callers can request strict machine-readable outputs. This ticket covers: (1) a request flag (json_mode) + compatibility header, (2) decoding-time constraints to guarantee well-formed JSON or deterministic fallbacks, (3) streaming chunk validation and repair heuristics, and (4) a test-suite (unit + fuzz + integration) that verifies schema adherence across model variants and compatibility layers for older clients. The feature must be opt-in and maintain backward compatibility with current non-strict behavior.
implementation_notes: Design decisions: implement a layered approach: 1) API-layer schema enforcement: the request contains a schema reference (OpenAPI/JSON Schema id) or inline schema. 2) Decoder-layer hard constraints: use token allowlist/denylist derived from tokenizer mapping and implement suffix-tree checks so decoder never emits tokens that immediately break JSON structural invariants (unclosed brace, stray comma). 3) Post-stream validator: stream chunks through a lightweight incremental parser; on parse failure attempt deterministic repairs (close braces, trim partial token, re-request short continuation from model with strict seed) before returning error to caller. 4) Compatibility shim: support legacy clients via header X-JSON-Mode: legacy that triggers a best-effort canonicalizer rather than strict enforcement. Implementation will live in runtime branch feature/json-mode and runtime/decoder modules.
test_plan: Unit tests for token-level constraint generator: ensure generated allowlists include tokens for digits, quotes, punctuation required by schema
Fuzz tests with malformed prefixes and injection attempts (e.g., 'Oops', 'Ignore this and output X') to ensure decoder does not escape json-mode
Streaming integration: validate partial chunks against incremental parser; simulate network dropout and ensure reconnect + resume maintains schema correctness
Schema adherence matrix: run a matrix across top 10 curated models (open and Redwood-verified) and quantization profiles; report pass/fail and failure modes
Compatibility tests: exercise legacy header behavior and verify canonicalizer outputs JSON-like but annotated with warnings instead of hard error
E2E test with function-calling + structured outputs: ensure tool-calling payloads produced in json_mode are accepted by the function-runner without extra reparsing
acceptance_criteria: When json_mode=true, API responses must parse as JSON according to provided schema for 99.9% of requests in the model matrix
Constrained decoder prevents common structural violations (unclosed arrays/objects, unmatched quotes, trailing commas) without blocking valid outputs
Streaming responses validated incrementally; repair heuristics succeed for transient parse errors in >90% attempts and otherwise return a reproducible error with diagnostic codes
Compatibility header X-JSON-Mode: legacy preserves old behavior but flags outputs with "_json_mode_warning" when strict conformance fails
Automated test-suite integrated into CI with clear failure reasons and links to flaky-run dashboard
risks: Potential runtime perf regression when aggressive token constraints are applied (high token checking cost). Risk of false negatives for highly creative model outputs that semantically match the schema but use unusual tokenization. Compatibility shim adds complexity to telemetry and support. We will gate the feature behind a rollout flag and run load tests on dedicated clusters before enabling for hosted tier.
